instruction: I work with long logs and need unlimited scrollback in my terminal. Enable unlimited scrollback permanently so I never lose command output history, even after reboot.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(1); pyautogui.write('gsettings get org.gnome.Terminal.Legacy.Profile:/org/gnome/terminal/legacy/profiles:/:$(gsettings get org.gnome.Terminal.ProfilesList default | tr -d "'")/ scrollback-unlimited'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.press('enter')

metadata.explanation: Task requires permanently enabling unlimited scrollback. Evaluator opens new terminal and checks scrollback-unlimited setting using gsettings, expecting 'true'. Uses existing check_include_exclude metric with vm_terminal_output getter.
metadata.similarity_to_original: high - same pattern of OS terminal configuration that persists across reboots
